name: rp_static_spread_carry_TLT_IEF_a
rationale: The NY Fed ACM 10-year term premium has returned to clearly positive territory in 2026 (0.79% as of 2026-07-30) after roughly five years near or below zero, and the long end has bear-steepened on Treasury supply and QT rather than on the expected short-rate path -- the 30-year cleared 5.25% in late July 2026 (highest since 2007) against a ~4.70% 10-year, a ~55bp 10s30s slope. A static always-on long-TLT/short-IEF spread is the plainest way to harvest that duration risk premium inside UNIVERSE: it holds the 20y+ sector against the 7-10y sector, gets paid the term-premium differential with no directional forecast, and bears the real risk that the same supply pressure pushes the premium higher still. Distinct from family N's DEAD pairs_cointegration row, which tested TLT/IEF as a mean-reverting spread (and dropped it at the ADF filter, never traded OOS); this is a structural carry bet on the spread's level, not on its reversion.
citation: Adrian, Crump & Moench (2013), 'Pricing the Term Structure with Linear Regressions', NY Fed ACM term premia (newyorkfed.org/research/data_indicators/term-premia-tabs) -- 10y ACM term premium 0.79% at 2026-07-30; 30y Treasury 5.25% vs 10y ~4.70% late July 2026 (mariemontcapital.com/fomc-minutes-july-2026/, primerates.com Treasury yield curve, ferrantecapitaladvisers.com/insights/treasury-term-premium-regime-2026/).

name: rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_SPY_GLD_252_252
rationale: Structural context, not a track-record claim: the equity-bond correlation that makes a rates leg the default hedge for an equity leg has flipped positive again in 2026. The late-February 2026 Strait of Hormuz closure delivered exactly the shock that produces that regime -- an oil-driven supply/inflation shock lifts discount rates, compressing equity valuations and Treasury prices at the same time, and US 10-year Treasury returns have been negative alongside equity selloffs since. Gold's demand base is structurally different from both: official-sector buying ran 244 tonnes in Q1 2026 (10th 200t+ quarter in 11), is explicitly strategic reserve diversification rather than rate- or dollar-sensitive flow, and gold's low-to-negative equity correlation has persisted specifically through geopolitical and oil-driven inflation episodes. That is the mechanism for these two legs to offset: SPY's trend leg is driven by the earnings/discount-rate channel, GLD's by an official-sector reserve-diversification and debasement-hedge channel with opposite-signed sensitivity to the same real-rate and inflation shocks -- not merely two things that happen to be uncorrelated. Both lookbacks are the canonical 12-month time-series-momentum horizon (Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen 2012), chosen for being the pre-existing standard rather than picked, and freq M matches that horizon's turnover. Stated honestly: each leg on its own is in the trend family this lab has already killed many times over, and the claim under test is only whether the cross-asset-class pairing earns its place under gate 2 while gate 1's DSR still requires the combination itself to beat a duty-cycle-matched null. Distinct from the only prior pipeline proposal (rp_static_spread_carry_TLT_IEF_a, a rates term-premium carry bet) in primitive, mechanism and asset classes.
citation: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012), 'Time Series Momentum', Journal of Financial Economics 104(2) -- source of the 12-month lookback. Equity-bond correlation regime and the late-Feb-2026 Strait of Hormuz trigger: Seeking Alpha, 'Stock-Bond Dynamics May Be In Flux, But Global Diversification Proved Its Worth In 2026' (seekingalpha.com/article/4916748); inflation >3% historically producing positive equity-bond correlation. Gold's persistent negative equity correlation through geopolitical and oil-driven inflation risk, and its elevated diversifier role when stock-bond correlation is high: State Street, 'Gold takes the diversification crown' and 'Gold 2026 Midyear Outlook' (ssga.com/us/en/intermediary/insights); World Gold Council, 'Why gold in 2026? A cross-asset perspective' (gold.org/goldhub/research/why-gold-2026-cross-asset-perspective). Official-sector demand of 244 tonnes in Q1 2026: World Gold Council, Gold Demand Trends Q1 2026 -- Central Banks (gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-demand-trends/gold-demand-trends-q1-2026/central-banks), released 2026-04-29.

name: rp_static_spread_carry_USO_DBC_a
rationale: Structural, not a track-record claim. The WTI futures curve has been in steep backwardation since the late-February 2026 Middle East supply shock and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, and stayed there through July even after the April 7 ceasefire -- December 2026 WTI has traded as much as $40 below May/June delivery. That is the live instance of a pre-existing structural claim, which is what this candidate actually tests: the hedging-pressure/normal-backwardation risk premium in commodity futures is concentrated at the FRONT of the curve, where producer hedging demand and curve slope are both greatest. The two UNIVERSE tickers separate exactly that exposure by construction, not by correlation: USO rolls front-month WTI and therefore sits fully on the front spread, while DBC's 'Optimum Yield' index rule deliberately searches out to 13 months for the best implied roll and so moves AWAY from the front few months, which Invesco's own methodology states is where the slope is steepest. A fixed, always-on long USO / short DBC is thus a static bet on the front-of-curve roll differential, hedging out most broad commodity beta, with no directional forecast of the oil price -- the same shape as this lab's one surviving carry book (crypto funding), where the return is compensation for bearing a real tail risk rather than a prediction. The risk borne is stated plainly and is severe: when the front of the curve flips to steep contango, front-month rolling produces the most negative roll yield available, and the OOS window (2018-present) contains April 2020, when exactly that happened to USO. The candidate should be expected to fail if that tail dominates the average premium; that is the hypothesis, not a caveat added after the fact. Distinct from family N's DEAD pairs_cointegration row, which tested USO/DBC as a mean-reverting spread and dropped it at the ADF filter (p=0.201) without ever trading OOS -- this is a structural bet on the spread's average drift, not on its reversion. Distinct in mechanism and asset class from both prior pipeline proposals (a rates term-premium carry and an equity/gold trend hedge). freq M matches the monthly futures roll cadence the mechanism operates on.
citation: Keynes' normal-backwardation / hedging-pressure premium and its concentration at the front of the curve: Gorton & Rouwenhorst (2006), 'Facts and Fantasies about Commodity Futures', Financial Analysts Journal 62(2); Erb & Harvey (2006), 'The Strategic and Tactical Value of Commodity Futures', FAJ 62(2), on roll return dominating commodity index returns. Current curve shape: CME Group, 'Implications of WTI Oil Futures In Backwardation Amid the Supply Crunch' (cmegroup.com/insights/economic-research/2026/) -- steep backwardation since the 2026-02-28 supply shock, persisting past the 2026-04-07 ceasefire, Dec-2026 WTI up to $40 below May/June delivery; CNBC, 'The oil market is in backwardation -- what it means for energy prices' (cnbc.com, 2026-03-26) and 'Oil prices fall as more tankers exit Strait of Hormuz' (cnbc.com, 2026-06-26). Roll-rule difference between the two legs: Invesco DB Commodity Index Tracking Fund (DBC) Optimum Yield methodology -- rolls to the contract within the next 13 months with the maximum implied roll yield, explicitly contrasted with front-month rolling because 'the slope of the curve tends to be steepest in the front few months' (invesco.com/us, DBC product documentation); United States Oil Fund (USO) holds near-month WTI futures.
